## Detailed Chronological Account of the Agent Failure

### The Task / Setup

The agent under analysis is **Claude Opus 4.6** running as the embedded LLM within the **OpenClaw** framework (version 2026.3.3), serving users via Discord. The user was running a workload involving **5+ concurrent sub-agent sessions** (all using Opus) alongside a main session. The main session was given a conversational turn that required tool calls (e.g., `exec`, `read`).

### Sequence of Events

1. **User sends a message** in the main Discord session that triggers the agent to invoke tool calls as part of its reasoning turn.

2. **Tool calls execute successfully.** The agent's tool invocations (exec, read, etc.) complete without error. The user can see the tool call results rendered in the Discord UI.

3. **Post-tool-call LLM API request is made.** After the tool calls return, the OpenClaw agent runner makes a follow-up API call to Claude Opus 4.6 to generate the assistant's text response synthesizing the tool results. This is the standard agentic loop: tools run → results are fed back to the model → model generates a final text reply.

4. **The API returns a 429 rate limit error.** Because the 5+ concurrent sub-agent Opus sessions had consumed the API quota, this follow-up LLM call is rejected with a rate limit error. The gateway logs record this clearly:
   - `[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.`
   - `[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=main error="FailoverError: ⚠️ API rate limit reached."`

5. **The error is silently swallowed.** The error handling code in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` processes the embedded agent run result. The `finalEmbeddedError` is set (with `isError=true`) and the payloads are empty (no text was generated). However, the post-run error guard **only checks for context overflow errors** (a fix from earlier issue #26905). The rate limit error does not match `isContextOverflowError`, so it falls through all the error checks.

6. **The code returns `kind: "success"` with no payload text.** Because the error was not caught, the execution path reaches the default return statement, which returns a "success" result with empty payloads. No text, no error message, nothing.

7. **The user sees a completely silent/empty assistant turn.** In the Discord UI, the tool call results are visible, but there is no assistant text response following them. No error message is displayed. The conversation appears stuck/dead. The user has no indication that anything went wrong or that they should retry.

### Key Signals and Feedback

- **Error was logged internally** — the gateway logs clearly captured `isError=true` and the rate limit message, but this information never propagated to the user-facing response.
- **The pre-tool-call error path worked correctly** — the code had a separate path (`"Embedded agent failed before reply"`) that properly handled rate limit errors when they occurred *before* any tool calls. The bug was specifically in the *mid-turn* path (after tool calls completed).
- **The root cause was an incomplete error guard** — issue #26905 had previously added handling for context overflow errors in this code path, but only that specific error type was checked. Rate limit (`isRateLimitErrorMessage`) and overload (`isOverloadedErrorMessage`) errors were not included, despite the helper functions already being available in the `pi-embedded-helpers` module.

### Aftermath: Attempted Fixes (None Merged)

Four separate PRs were submitted within hours of the issue being filed (March 5, 2026), all targeting the same file:

| PR | Author | Submitted | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| #36143 | JaewookYou (issue reporter) | 12:55 UTC | Automated reviewers flagged issues (overload errors mislabeled as rate limit; missing post-turn flush cleanup). Auto-closed as stale on April 20. |
| #36169 | Sid-Qin | 13:11 UTC | Closed by maintainer `thewilloftheshadow` on March 6. |
| #36193 | RealKai42 | 13:28 UTC | Closed by maintainer `thewilloftheshadow` on March 6. |
| #36206 | openperf | 13:37 UTC | Most comprehensive fix (added cleanup flush, bounded timeout, catch-all). Addressed all automated review feedback successfully. Closed by barnacle bot: "author has more than 10 active PRs in this repo." |

**None of the four PRs were merged.** The issue itself was marked stale on April 17 and auto-closed by the barnacle bot on April 22, 2026, with the status "not planned." At least one additional PR (#47046) was later submitted referencing this issue, also closed.

### Final Outcome

The bug — Claude Opus 4.6 producing a **completely silent, empty response** when a rate limit hits mid-turn after tool calls — was reported, diagnosed with a clear root cause, received multiple fix attempts (some with thorough review integration), but **was never resolved**. The issue was closed due to inactivity by an automated stale-bot, not because the underlying problem was fixed.

{"body":"### Summary

This PR fixes **[#36142](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/36142 )**, where the assistant returns a silent, empty response if an LLM API error (like rate-limiting or overload) occurs mid-turn after tool calls have already completed.

The previous behavior provided no feedback to the user, making the conversation appear stuck. This fix extends the error handling established in [#26905](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/26905 ) to gracefully manage these mid-turn failures.

### Problem

When a rate limit (429), overload, or other API error occurs after tool calls, the agent run terminates with an embedded error but no payload text. The existing error handling in `agent-runner-execution.ts` only checked for context overflow, causing other errors to be silently swallowed.

### Solution

This solution enhances the post-run error handling in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` to provide a more robust and user-friendly experience:

1.  **Differentiated Error Handling**: The code now specifically checks for rate-limit and overload errors in addition to the existing context overflow check, providing distinct, informative messages for each case.

2.  **Robust Mid-Turn Cleanup**: For errors that occur mid-turn (i.e., after tool calls have been dispatched), this PR introduces a crucial cleanup step. Before returning the final error payload, it ensures the `blockReplyPipeline` is flushed and all `pendingToolTasks` are awaited. This guarantees that any partial results or tool outputs generated before the error are properly delivered and not lost, preventing potential race conditions and data inconsistencies.

3.  **Generic Fallback**: A generic fallback handler has been added to catch any other embedded errors that occur mid-turn, ensuring that the agent never fails silently. The error message is sanitized for user safety.

## Detailed Chronological Account of the Agent Failure

### The Task / Setup

The agent under analysis is **Claude Opus 4.6** running as the embedded LLM within the **OpenClaw** framework (version 2026.3.3), serving users via Discord. The user was running a workload involving **5+ concurrent sub-agent sessions** (all using Opus) alongside a main session. The main session was given a conversational turn that required tool calls (e.g., `exec`, `read`).

### Sequence of Events

1. **User sends a message** in the main Discord session that triggers the agent to invoke tool calls as part of its reasoning turn.

2. **Tool calls execute successfully.** The agent's tool invocations (exec, read, etc.) complete without error. The user can see the tool call results rendered in the Discord UI.

3. **Post-tool-call LLM API request is made.** After the tool calls return, the OpenClaw agent runner makes a follow-up API call to Claude Opus 4.6 to generate the assistant's text response synthesizing the tool results. This is the standard agentic loop: tools run → results are fed back to the model → model generates a final text reply.

4. **The API returns a 429 rate limit error.** Because the 5+ concurrent sub-agent Opus sessions had consumed the API quota, this follow-up LLM call is rejected with a rate limit error. The gateway logs record this clearly:
   - `[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: isError=true error=⚠️ API rate limit reached.`

5. **The error is silently swallowed.** The error handling code in `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution.ts` processes the embedded agent run result. The `finalEmbeddedError` is set (with `isError=true`) and the payloads are empty (no text was generated). However, the post-run error guard **only checks for context overflow errors** (a fix from earlier issue #26905). The rate limit error does not match `isContextOverflowError`, so it falls through all the error checks.

7. **The user sees a completely silent/empty assistant turn.** In the Discord UI, the tool call results are visible, but there is no assistant text response following them. No error message is displayed. The conversation appears stuck/dead. The user has no indication that anything went wrong or that they should retry.

### Key Signals and Feedback

- **Error was logged internally** — the gateway logs clearly captured `isError=true` and the rate limit message, but this information never propagated to the user-facing response.

Rate limit (`isRateLimitErrorMessage`) and overload (`isOverloadedErrorMessage`) errors were not included, despite the helper functions already being available in the `pi-embedded-helpers` module.
